verdict.rationale: OpenCode supports trigger-based autonomous fixes through its GitHub integration: mentioning /opencode or /oc in a comment runs it in a GitHub Actions runner, where it works on a new branch and submits a PR. Headless building blocks (`opencode run`, `opencode serve`, the SDK, and `--auto` permission approval) make unattended runs possible, but always-on scheduling would have to be assembled by the user with external tools like cron or Actions schedules. Missing for 10: native scheduled/cron agents, non-comment event triggers (e.g., CI failure or issue-opened), a documented always-on maintenance agent mode, and independent corroboration of reliable unattended operation.
